MARKS-AND-BRANDS-RECORD-RECOVERY-01.quote: Read the index headings and arrangement before searching by the owner's surname. A design initial can be the filing key: the teaching example finds an owner under the letter beginning the brand, rather than the owner's surname.

MISSING-MARRIAGE-JURISDICTION-SEARCH-01.quote: A verified original that resolves the marriage ends the search. Otherwise the search is not finished, and the gap is not reported, until every ranked candidate has been searched or recorded as unavailable.

MUSCOVITE-CENSUS-SETTLER-ORIGIN-RECOVERY.quote: Every stated origin is kept as testimony until a matching departure-side entry is found.

MYHERITAGE-DNA-MATCH-INVESTIGATION-01.quote: Save empty results with their actual query, kit, filters and date. Do not fill an unshown DNA measurement with zero or infer that a person outside the list has no shared DNA.

MYHERITAGE-HISTORICAL-RECORD-SEARCH-01.quote: Preserve the sparse baseline before tightening it. If a tighter query fails, relax one condition at a time and record the reason; changing everything together conceals what excluded the record.

NAZI-ERA-ANCESTRY-PROOF-RECORDS-01.quote: Their racial categories are the regime's classifications and are never evidence of anything about a person. Their entries were copied from parish and civil registers and must be checked against those registers.

NEWSPAPERS-COM-SEARCH-RECOVERY-01.quote: A surname can occur in one item and a travel verb in another on the same page. Confirm the subject and event within the actual item before assigning that event to the searched person.

OLD-BELIEVER-SECTARIAN-RECORD-RECOVERY-0.quote: Use this recipe when a Russian-Empire family suspected of Old Belief (раскол, старообрядчество) or Edinoverie (единоверие) is missing from the ordinary Orthodox metrical books, revision lists or confession rolls. Do not conclude that the family went unrecorded.

ORTHODOX-CLERGY-RECORD-RECOVERY-01.quote: Use it before you search metrical books or a present-day oblast archive, and before you merge or split clergy who share a surname.

PERIODICAL-INDEX-SEARCH-RETRIEVAL-01.quote: A personal-name miss therefore usually means the article text was never searched, and a hit is only a citation.

POLISH-INDEX-ORIGINAL-RECORD-RECOVERY-01.quote: A register description establishes a lead to holdings, not that the target entry has been inspected. Preserve the complete reference, not just a short number detached from its archive and fonds.

PORTUGUESE-PARISH-CIVIL-REGISTER-RECOVER.quote: Use it before you treat Portuguese records like Spanish or Hispanic ones. That mistake leads to four failures: searching a civil register that did not cover the person, looking in the wrong archive, reading the first surname as the father's, and calling a book missing when another archive holds it.

PROBATE-CASE-DOCUMENT-INVENTORY-01.quote: Keep a case inventory and a queue of unresolved references, so finding one useful document does not silently finish the estate search.

PUBLISHED-BOOK-CATALOGUE-AND-FULL-TEXT-D.quote: A miss is only a miss for that tool, query and range. It never establishes that the book doesn't exist or isn't held.

QUAKER-MEETING-RECORD-RECOVERY-01.quote: Before relying on Hinshaw, check that it covers the meeting. Decode the entry's meeting before you assign it to a place.

RABBINIC-LITERATURE-PERSON-SEARCH-01.quote: Keep two questions apart: did the ancestor exist, and is the bridge from your person to that ancestor documented? Rabbinic books often answer the first and rarely prove the second.

REPOSITORY-PHOTOGRAPH-COLLECTION-SEARCH-.quote: Do not compare faces yourself and do not name anyone from appearance. Resemblance is never evidence on its own: a recognition stays an attributed claim until documents support it.

RESEARCH-DOCUMENTATION-01.quote: Use `NIL` for a completed search with no hits. Record inaccessible images, interrupted searches and unsearched collections with their actual status.

ROOTSMAGIC-TREE-RECONCILIATION-WORKFLOW-.quote: Choose the destination and operation for each object, then inspect the saved result.

RUSSIAN-EMPIRE-EMIGRANT-ORIGIN-RECOVERY-.quote: Preserve the wording and field role until the movement and locality evidence resolve them.

RUSSIAN-EMPIRE-JEWISH-IDENTITY-ATTRIBUTI.quote: **A name mismatch never changes the branch verdict on its own; the household chain does.** Chain the person through household number → previous household number → age at previous revision → "выбыло" column → additional lists before you interpret any name.

RUSSIAN-EMPIRE-JEWISH-METRICAL-BOOK-RECO.quote: Do not search for "the village's" or "the synagogue's" metrical book. Having synagogues, or a sizeable Jewish population, does not show that a place had its own crown rabbi.

RUSSIAN-ESTATE-REGISTRATION-STATUS-01.quote: **A town mark on мещанин or купец names the society of registration, not the birthplace or residence.**

RUSSIAN-HOUSEHOLD-LIST-TRANSCRIPTION-AUD.quote: **Record what the image says, even against other years.**

RUSSIAN-IMPERIAL-SERVICE-RECORD-RECOVERY.quote: Do not stop at metrical books, revision lists or a military archive. A man in state service had his career and family written up in a formulary or service list (формулярный / послужной список).

RUSSIAN-MILITARY-REPRESSION-RECORD-EPISO.quote: an award order after a missing report does not, by itself, establish survival between those dates. Obtain an event-specific source before extending a life or death interval.

RUSSIAN-ORTHODOX-CONFESSION-LIST-READING.quote: The common errors are to read one year as a census, to turn an age into a birth year, to treat a household number as an identifier, and to treat a list entry as proof of a marriage, a parent or a death.

RUSSIAN-ORTHODOX-METRICAL-BOOK-RECOVERY-.quote: Read marriage-count formulae literally, treat margin decrees as separate dated events, and treat names and patronymics as hypotheses rather than proof of descent.

RUSSIAN-REVISION-LIST-HOUSEHOLD-CHAINING.quote: Record each copy as a separate observation of one episode, never as corroboration.

RUSSIAN-VILLAGE-FAMILY-RECONSTITUTION-01.quote: **A surname is a hint, not an identifier.**

RUSSIAN-VOLOST-TOWN-ADMINISTRATION-RECOR.quote: The common mistake is to send the researcher only to church registers and revision lists. That misses the local administrative fonds.

SCANDINAVIAN-PARISH-RECORD-RECOVERY-01.quote: Follow the family by farm or residence and by page cross-reference, not by patronymic. Settle identity at the household level.

SCANDINAVIAN-PATRONYMIC-FARM-NAME-RECORD.quote: The name in the parish register is usually not the American surname. Same-named parishioners are common, so separate them by birth date, parents, spouse, farm and vaccination entries, never by name alone.

SCHOOL-UNIVERSITY-RECORD-RECOVERY-01.quote: A compiled or published list is a lead with limited coverage. Absence from it does not show that the person never attended.

SCOTTISH-PARISH-STATUTORY-RECORD-RECOVER.quote: Treat register gaps and unsearched denominations as coverage still to search, not as proof the event did not happen.

SOURCE-CITATION-01.quote: An index entry and an inspected original image have different retrieval paths; record which one you used.

SOVIET-PERSONAL-FILE-RECOVERY-01.quote: Keep questionnaires (анкеты) and autobiographies found there as dated self-reports, and keep catalogue hits found by name as candidates.

SPANISH-CIVIL-PARISH-RECORD-ROUTING-01.quote: **Expect the national Registro Civil only from 1 January 1871.**

STATE-LEGISLATIVE-PRIVATE-ACT-PETITIONS-.quote: search the state's index of legislative acts, gather every entry that shares the hit's locator, and then retrieve the act and the petition or application behind it.

SURNAME-DISTRIBUTION-LOCALITY-LEADS-01.quote: It turns time-sliced maps, attestation dictionaries, a couple's surname overlap and country-wide counts into a **ranked, bounded list of localities to search**. It never produces an origin finding.

SWEDISH-MILITARY-RECORD-ROUTING-01.quote: Swedish military records are not one searchable pool. Each index covers one series, one branch and one period, so classify the man first and read every miss against the coverage of the index you searched.

TAX-ROLL-OBSERVATION-WORKFLOW-01.quote: Check each year against the liability rules in force then, and record every change as a bounded interval.

UK-CENSUS-AND-1939-REGISTER-INTERPRETATI.quote: Before reading any value, settle what that year's image is, who wrote the value, what night or day it refers to and what the year covers.

UNKNOWN-PARENTAGE-WATO-01.quote: WATO assumes single-path descent. Pedigree collapse / endogamy / a match related through two lines silently invalidates the score — the tool has no way to know and will still rank confidently.

WATO-01.quote: **The output is a set of competing hypotheses with *relative* odds — never a verdict.**

WATO-04.quote: When interpreting a reported ranking, ask whether pedigree collapse, endogamy or more than one relationship path could apply to these matches; do not replace the question with a generic warning.

US-20TH-CENTURY-MILITARY-SERVICE-RECONST.quote: Do not claim that the records burned and nothing survives.

US-CENSUS-PRACTICAL-WORKFLOWS-01.quote: Preserve the original census locator and keep literal observations separate from calculations and proposed identities.

US-CHURCH-RECORD-CUSTODY-01.quote: Before searching, work out the exact denominational branch, the record types that branch kept, the congregation or minister who kept the entry, and who holds those registers now. Do not report "not found" or "records lost" until that custody path has been checked.

US-CIVIL-WAR-SERVICE-RECORD-EPISODES-01.quote: It prevents four common errors: treating registration as service, giving the soldier every battle his regiment fought, guessing a transfer's date or meaning, and treating a database miss as proof of non-service.

US-FEDERAL-COURT-CASE-FILE-RECOVERY-01.quote: Decide whether the matter is federal before you search a county courthouse or a large genealogy database.

US-FEDERAL-LAND-ENTRY-FILE-RECOVERY-01.quote: The digitized GLO item is the final grant or warrant image, often a single page. It is not the entry file.

US-FREEDPEOPLE-RECORD-RECOVERY-01.quote: Surname, enslaver, list order and DNA signals stay separate hypotheses until a record names the person.

US-MILITARY-PENSION-FILE-RECOVERY-01.quote: Preserve the distinction between an index, a service record, a pension file and an abbreviated copy product.

US-MILITARY-SERVICE-TYPE-RECORD-ROUTING-.quote: The usual failure is to search only federal compiled-service or pension indexes and then report "no service". A related mistake is reading an empty donation-land or bounty-land search as meaningful when the man was never eligible.

US-PERIOD-LAW-RECORD-READING-01.quote: A rule shows what was required or allowed. It does not show what happened in one family.

US-TRIBAL-ENROLLMENT-RECORD-RECOVERY-01.quote: A rejection alone neither shows nor rules out Native descent.

US-VITAL-REGISTRATION-COVERAGE-01.quote: The usual mistake is to treat the statewide mandate year as the first year of coverage, search one certificate index for one county, and report a negative. Before any absence statement, build a register with one row for each registration authority and each separate series.

USA-IMMIGRATION-SEARCH-RECOVERY-01.quote: The recurring mistake is treating a search miss as a missing ancestor when the failure lies in the selected port, date, recorded name, image, citizenship history or custodian.

WIKITREE-DNA-TESTER-LINKS-01.quote: Do not mark a relationship DNA-confirmed solely because a tester appears in a list or because the external tree link works.

XDNA-PHASING-JUDGMENT-01.quote: **Ban invented small-segment statistics.** Any false-positive-rate or chance-match number must be attributed to a specific company/study (23andMe 2014, AncestryDNA 2020, FTDNA's Family Finder Matching 5.0) — never a smoothed or averaged figure presented as a universal law.

YDNA-MTDNA-INTERPRETATION-01.quote: **you do not compute or assign haplogroups, TMRCAs, or NPE verdicts from your own reasoning.** Every such value is a *hypothesis to route to the right tool or corroborate* — never a fact to state.

Y-01.quote: A GD is *stochastic*, not a clock (below).

Y-02.quote: **you do not compute or assign haplogroups, TMRCAs, or NPE verdicts from your own reasoning.**

23ANDME-MATCH-RESEARCH-01.quote: The expensive mistake is assuming that every visible DNA Relative can be compared in every position, every percentage is autosomal-only, and every Download button returns the same kind of evidence.

ADMIXTURE-MODEL-RUN-SCOPE-01.quote: Nothing in this recipe establishes an ancestor, an origin locality or a relationship. A result that disagrees with a documented pedigree may make a candidate less likely. It never rules one out.

AGENT-RESEARCH-PROJECT-01.quote: Treat a model-written summary, tag or "key insight" as a pointer. Open the source before writing a claim.

AI-FOR-DNA-RESEARCH-01.quote: Never ask the LLM to compute relationship probabilities from a cM number — it *fabricates* them. Route a *single* cM figure to the **Shared cM Project / DNA Painter's Shared cM Tool** (point cM → the *range* of candidate relationships); if you have a tree plus multiple matches to place, that's **WATO** — a *different* DNA Painter tool that scores hypothesis slots, not a cM→relationship lookup.

CM-01.quote: Never ask the LLM to compute relationship probabilities from a cM number — it *fabricates* them.

CM-02.quote: Either way, always ask for **all** candidate relationships, never a single point answer.

AI-FOR-DOCUMENTARY-RECORDS-01.quote: **Every AI output is a hypothesis to verify against the original record, never a fact to file.**

AMSTERDAM-ARCHIVAL-RECORD-RECOVERY-01.quote: Read the entry by its register type, not by the index label.

ANCESTRY-DNA-MATCH-INVESTIGATION-01.quote: Keep three columns: observed cM, dated label with its origin, and sourced pedigree path.

ANCESTRY-RECORD-SEARCH-RECOVERY-01.quote: Keep three observations separate: no indexed candidate; no matching images in the available inventory; and documented absence in the original surviving records.

ARCHIVAL-IMAGE-COVERAGE-VERIFICATION-01.quote: A completed reader session establishes execution coverage, not transcription accuracy. A new surname was not searched merely because its pages occurred in an earlier sweep for other names.

AUSTRALIA-NZ-RECORD-ROUTING-01.quote: **Do not send a Port Phillip or Moreton Bay event to New South Wales because it predates separation.** Today's Victorian or Queensland index is the first stop.

AUSTRIAN-CONFESSIONAL-REGISTER-ROUTING-0.quote: **Do not read a Catholic baptism or burial as proof of non-Jewish origin.**

BEIDER-GIVEN-NAME-VARIANTS-01.quote: Two forms in one dictionary article create search candidates; they do not establish that two records describe the same person.

BESSARABIA-MOLDOVA-RECORD-ROUTING-01.quote: **Route by date and district, not by the word "Bessarabia".**

BRAZILIAN-PARISH-CIVIL-REGISTRY-RECOVERY.quote: **Work out the history of the place first.** Many Brazilian municipalities are recent. The town in a record may have been a village or district of an older municipality on the event date [S1].

BRITISH-COLONIAL-SLAVE-REGISTERS-01.quote: **Mark each return as a full list or a change return before reading it.**

BURIAL-EVIDENCE-PACKET-01.quote: Keep death, burial, inscription and database statements distinguishable. The result is a packet another researcher can inspect, with missing fields and unresolved discrepancies visible.

BUR-01.quote: Keep death, burial, inscription and database statements distinguishable.

BUR-02.quote: identity or conflicting-date conclusions belong to evidence-proof-judgment.

CANADIAN-CENSUS-INTERPRETATION-01.quote: For any census from 1871 onward, write on the observation that the enumeration was de jure. People were listed where they were supposed to belong, as reported by an informant, not where they physically were at a cutoff time.

CANADIAN-PROVINCIAL-RECORD-ROUTING-01.quote: Vital registration is provincial. Each province has its own start date, gaps and archive cut-off, so build one coverage row per province before you search.

CATHOLIC-PARISH-DIOCESAN-RECORD-RECOVERY.quote: State negative results only for the holdings you actually inspected.

CATHOLIC-SACRAMENTAL-CROSS-NOTATIONS-01.quote: The marriage entry's statement of where each party was baptized, and the marriage note later added to the baptism entry, appear only on the original page. Read both directions.

CHECHEN-INGUSH-1944-DEPORTATION-RECORDS-.quote: **Do not predict a file's absence from Grozny's war losses.**

CHINESE-LINEAGE-JIAPU-RECORDS-01.quote: Do not convert a Western spelling into one Pinyin character.

CITY-DIRECTORY-OBSERVATION-WORKFLOW-01.quote: A gap in a database's editions and an absent entry on inspected pages are different results. Neither alone establishes why the person is missing.

CONVICT-TRANSPORTATION-RECORD-CHAIN-01.quote: Each episode comes from its own record series, has its own locator and has its own date role. One index entry never stands for the whole chain.

CORPUS-SEEDED-NAME-SEARCH-01.quote: A completed zero-hit query describes that query and scope; it does not exclude a person whose record or spelling has not been tested.

COURT-CASE-FILE-RECOVERY-01.quote: Captions, arrests, index entries and case-law searches stay bounded leads.

CRIMINAL-COURT-PRISON-RECORD-RECOVERY-01.quote: Before choosing where to search for court files, establish which court tried the case and who holds the records now.

DEED-CONTENT-RELATIONSHIP-CLUES-01.quote: Every clue here is a dated hypothesis with a stated corroboration need. None is a kinship finding.

DESCENDANCY-GAP-WORKLIST-01.quote: An empty field leaves the event unresolved in this tree. It does not mean the event never happened.

DNA-COMPARISON-CONTROLS-01.quote: If the expected positive is missing, investigate the query, selection and processing before interpreting an empty list.

DNA-MATCH-OUTREACH-STAGING-01.quote: If consent is missing or unclear, stop at the contact plan and a draft for the tester to review. Do not choose recipients yourself.

OUT-01.quote: The letter must not state the conclusion.

OUT-02.quote: If consent is missing or unclear, stop at the contact plan and a draft for the tester to review.

DNAPAINTER-PRACTICAL-DNA-WORKFLOWS-01.quote: A copied segment belongs to its original comparison; an intersection is coordinate geometry; an inferred interval is a deduction; the Coverage Estimator is a pedigree-based estimate. Keep those outputs distinguishable.

DUTCH-CIVIL-CHURCH-RECORD-RECOVERY-01.quote: A failed search on WieWasWie or Open Archieven (openarchieven.nl) does not show that the event is missing from the municipality's records.

EARLY-NEW-ENGLAND-TOWN-RECORDS-01.quote: **Never report "not in the town records" without the coverage behind it.** Name the towns, volumes and page ranges actually read, and the volumes not read.

ELIB-UKRAINIAN-ARCHIVE-REFERENCE-BOOKS-0.quote: Prefer the current card's link over a constructed URL. A constructed route is a retrieval lead until its response is verified as the intended PDF; redirects, error HTML or an access failure leave acquisition unresolved.

ENGLAND-WALES-GRO-INDEX-RECOVERY-01.quote: These entries tell you the registration quarter, district, volume/page and, in the GRO birth index, the mother's maiden surname. They do not give an event date, a birthplace, a pairing of spouses or parentage.

ENGLISH-NONREGISTER-RECORD-RECOVERY-01.quote: Record which series do not cover the case. The register being silent does not make the question unanswerable.

ETHNICITY-ESTIMATE-VERSION-COMPARISON-01.quote: The tester's DNA did not change between versions; the vendor's method did. Ask first what the vendor changed, not what changed in the family [S11].

EVIDENCE-PROOF-JUDGMENT-01.quote: **You rule on identity and proof. The model assembles and drafts — it never concludes.**

PROOF-01.quote: **You rule on identity and proof. The model assembles and drafts — it never concludes.**

PROOF-02.quote: **Keep same-name candidates in SEPARATE research projects** so their records never cross-contaminate.

PROOF-03.quote: A converged match is evidence in the proof argument, not proof by itself.

PROOF-04.quote: **Include a search that challenges the preferred version.**

FAMILY-COLLECTION-INTAKE-AND-CAPTURE-01.quote: The common mistake is to optimize for tidy files. The model renames files by person, re-orders items, scans fronts only, imposes one resolution or format, treats a received crop or a stitched assembly as the master, and assumes an export kept the captions. Each of those destroys part of the record that later identification depends on: who held the item, the order it arrived in, its reverse, and the surfaces nobody has inspected yet.

FAMILY-INTERVIEWS-AND-ORAL-TRADITION-01.quote: A correctly recorded recollection remains an account to assess, not an automatic tree fact.

ORAL-01.quote: Before a new recording starts, explain the topic, who will hear the recording and how it may be used, and get the participant's consent.

ORAL-02.quote: With a photograph, ask about the vehicles, buildings, place and season before asking who the people are, and never supply a desired identity [S2].

FAMILY-PAPERS-AND-BIBLE-REGISTER-DATING-.quote: A postmark dates the mailing. It is the latest possible date for the writing and for any event the text reports as already past, but it does not date those events: a birth, death, visit or move reported inside a card needs its own date [S1].

FAMILY-PHOTOGRAPH-ATTRIBUTION-AND-DATING.quote: record each identification as an attributed claim with its basis, turn every clue into an earliest or latest bound, and test an attribution against the documented lifetime of the person named, never against faces.

PHOTO-01.quote: Preserve the attribution and its basis; do not identify a person by their face or compare faces across photographs.

PHOTO-02.quote: Before you upload a private family photograph to any outside service (reverse image search, enhancement or colorization), answer the privacy gate in `SKILL.md` and get the user's explicit permission for that service.

FAMILYSEARCH-PRACTICAL-RECORD-WORKFLOWS-.quote: Confirm candidates from the image and context. A name appearing in text does not establish the candidate's identity.

FRENCH-BELGIAN-CIVIL-ACT-EXTRACTION-01.quote: Store two fields: the act date, and the event date as stated (literal) or as resolved. Never fill only one date field.

FRENCH-CANADIAN-REGISTER-RECOVERY-01.quote: Do not call the person absent until the name forms are exhausted

FRENCH-DEPARTMENTAL-RECORD-ROUTING-01.quote: **Send each search to an Archives départementales (AD), not to a national index.** Older civil registers, census lists, military registers, Enregistrement tables and notarial minutes are kept by the AD, each with its own website and series.

FTDNA-PRACTICAL-DNA-WORKFLOWS-01.quote: A match name is a join key, not a unique person identifier. Matching Bucket and Linked Relationship are values observed at download. Record link changes separately from the retrieval date, keep the export choice and kit with the rows, and refresh match metadata after relinking.

GALICIA-BUKOVINA-HABSBURG-RECORD-ROUTING.quote: **Start an ethnic Ukrainian villager in Galicia in Greek Catholic books, not Orthodox ones.**

GEDCOM-RESEARCH-EXPORT-01.quote: The recipe prevents seven failures: changing the header version and calling the file converted, attaching a child to the father's wife because she shares his family record, turning a shared patronymic and surname into a parent link, reading QUAY as a research status, silently converting an Old Style date or padding an approximate year, culling or confirming a supplied tree's claims during a format change, and marking people deceased so that they can go into a shared file.

GED-01.quote: **Never mark anyone deceased from a birth-year cutoff or a missing death date** in order to export, share or publish them.

GED-02.quote: **Apply the living-person rules to a copy prepared for sharing.**

GED-03.quote: **Never map QUAY to or from a research status.**

GED-04.quote: For an online destination, identify living or possibly living people and keep the upload conditional on each one's explicit permission for that destination or on leaving that person out completely (section 8).

GED-05.quote: A supplied `QUAY 3` and a source title or research note saying "unverified" are not contradictory merely because of that research-status wording.

GEDMATCH-PRACTICAL-DNA-WORKFLOWS-01.quote: A match-list row, a pairwise segment, a shared-match list, a triangulation result and a generated kit answer different questions. Keep their tool, inputs and settings attached to every result.

GM-01.quote: Authorization to analyze a kit is not permission to upload it.

GM-02.quote: require that person's explicit permission for GEDmatch and the chosen option.

GM-03.quote: For an upload request, make the gate explicit in the first reply: ask whether the file is the user's own test or someone else's, distinguish permission to access or analyze it from permission to transfer it, and ask about permission for GEDmatch and the chosen visibility and law-enforcement matching options.

GENEALOGY-STANDARDS-AUDIT-01.quote: A populated log, polished footnote or completed checklist does not establish the Genealogical Proof Standard (GPS). The researcher owns the final ruling on evidentiary sufficiency.

GENI-PRACTICAL-RESEARCH-WORKFLOWS-01.quote: Distinguish tree assertions, source-supported statements, pending requests and completed changes. Draft any manager or curator request for my review; do not send it.

GEORGIA-TEXAS-STATE-LAND-GRANT-RECOVERY-.quote: Do not read a missing name in a later lottery as proof that the person did not register, was not eligible or was not a resident.

GERMAN-COMPENSATION-FILE-RECOVERY-01.quote: The hit tells you a file exists for one indexed applicant or injured party. It does not tell you who filed the claim, which relatives the file names, or whether the indexed person is yours.

GERMAN-EMIGRANT-ORIGIN-SOURCES-01.quote: The main mistake to avoid is treating a miss in official emigration-permission files or a regional index as proof that the person did not come from that state.

GERMAN-LOCAL-CENSUS-REGISTRATION-RECOVER.quote: "No census here" ends that route only. Follow it with the other headings and the next archive.

GERMAN-MILITARY-RECORD-PERIOD-ROUTING-01.quote: A regimental canton, a gazette notice or a casualty-list line is a lead with limits. None of them is a birthplace, a death date or an identity.

GERMAN-OFFICIAL-GAZETTE-NOTICE-SEARCH-01.quote: Each notice is a dated act by a named authority. It does not show that the person lived in the gazette's district. It does not prove that anyone left, and it does not confirm anyone's identity.

GERMAN-REGISTER-IMAGE-RECOVERY-01.quote: **Narrow by the Kreis, Oberamt or state nesting.** Many towns share a name.

HEBREWBOOKS-SEARCH-RECOVERY-01.quote: An access error, an unsubmitted query and a completed search with zero hits are different observations. Record the surface and the observation before interpreting it.

HISPANIC-CATHOLIC-REGISTER-RECOVERY-01.quote: **Never copy a baptism date into the birth field.** Baptism could be late because of distance, the priest's fee or inertia [S2].

HISTORIC-HUNGARY-RECORD-ROUTING-01.quote: **For local registers outside today's Hungary, start with the successor state's archive.** Inside Hungary, check the parish for pre-1895 church books, the MNL in Budapest for films of those books [S20 @2026-11-16], and the county archive for second copies [S21 @2026-11-16].

HISTORICAL-MAP-RECORD-RECOVERY-01.quote: retain the map-to-case link as a candidate until the records establish it. Keep the estimated map-production date, the case-file span and any dated event statements separate. Seek the case's actual statements before dating the depicted event or moving a same-named person to another generation.

HISTORICAL-PLACE-NAME-RESOLUTION-01.quote: The recipe lists every same-named feature in feature-level, period-dated gazetteers, keeps the name exactly as written, and lets other dated evidence about the person choose among the candidates.

HOLOCAUST-TESTIMONY-SOURCE-INTERPRETATIO.quote: Recover the information behind a Yad Vashem name result without converting a memorial submission, archival list or evacuation entry into an unsupported death or family conclusion.

ILLEGITIMACY-RECORD-RECOVERY-01.quote: A bond, court file or church-court suit records an accusation, a reputation or a court outcome. It does not prove biological fatherhood.

IMMIGRANT-CONGREGATION-ORIGIN-RECORDS-01.quote: One hometown statement in one entry is a lead. Before filing identity, correlate it with the rest of the family's evidence and with origin-side records.

INSTITUTIONAL-PATIENT-RECORD-RECOVERY-01.quote: Never treat a refusal, a form letter or a court-order requirement as evidence that no file exists. Log it as an access outcome and switch to the court and newspaper routes below.

IRISH-1901-1911-CENSUS-RETURNS-01.quote: Only a townland that has returns, searched by all the routes in steps 1–2 and browsed house by house, supports "not found in [townland], [year]".

IRISH-CATHOLIC-PARISH-IMAGE-RECOVERY-01.quote: Carry an Irish Catholic baptism or marriage lead into the National Library of Ireland's register images, inspect the actual entry and preserve the register and image locators. A transcription can identify a parish and date without supplying an image; a baptism date remains a baptism date unless the original separately records birth.

IRISH-CIVIL-REGISTRATION-JURISDICTION-RE.quote: Births are registered after they happen, so put the quarter in its own field. Take the event date only from the certificate.

IRISH-EMIGRANT-ORIGIN-LOCALITY-01.quote: Do not record a townland as the origin on a place-name, surname-distribution or farm-name match alone. Submit the person-specific evidence that ties this person to the townland, from destination or Irish records, and leave the identity ruling to the researcher.

IRISH-LAND-VALUATION-OCCUPANCY-SERIES-01.quote: Read each one as a dated list of occupiers and holdings. None of them is a household census.

IRISH-PROBATE-AND-DEED-RECOVERY-01.quote: **Do not read an entry as proof that the will survives.** The entry records the grant, not the document's survival; check the copy lanes in step 3.

ITALIAN-STATO-CIVILE-PARISH-RECORD-RECOV.quote: Fix who registered the event before you choose a series. Use the event year and the place's ruler in that year, not today's region.

JAPANESE-KOSEKI-HONSEKI-RECOVERY-01.quote: One spoken reading can be written with many kanji combinations, so a romanized name does not identify the person. The request needs the exact registered Japanese spelling, kanji or kana as recorded ([Kagoshima City naming FAQ](https://www.city.kagoshima.lg.jp/faq-kurashi/shimin/q113.html)).

JEWISH-ARCHIVAL-LIST-TRIAGE-01.quote: A geographical association does not establish either Jewish contents or the identity of a person. Do not present a title match as a verified Jewish list.

JEWISH-GENEALOGY-CONDITIONAL-HYPOTHESES-.quote: A proposed father can select a search town; establishing that father still does not establish the child's birthplace, the intended namesake or the ancestor behind every shared segment.

JEWISHGEN-SEARCH-FAMILY-RECONSTRUCTION-0.quote: Do not convert a phonetic, household or age match into a relationship.

LAND-INDEX-BOOK-SERIES-RECOVERY-01.quote: Keep both index directions, the instrument and recording dates, and the original locator visible, so one missed surname entry or guessed book does not become a false absence.

LOCAL-REPOSITORY-UNCATALOGUED-HOLDINGS-0.quote: Treat an empty catalogue or online search as covering only the repository's processed, catalogued holdings. Do not write "not held", "nothing found" or "searched [repository]" on the strength of it.

MANUSCRIPT-COLLECTION-RECOVERY-01.quote: A personal-name search that finds nothing is therefore not a finding. Never report "no manuscripts exist" or "not in this archive" because a name search failed [S1], [S3], [S21].

MARKS-AND-BRANDS-RECORD-RECOVERY-01.quote: Read the index headings and arrangement before searching by the owner's surname. A design initial can be the filing key: the teaching example finds an owner under the letter beginning the brand, rather than the owner's surname.

MISSING-MARRIAGE-JURISDICTION-SEARCH-01.quote: A verified original that resolves the marriage ends the search. Otherwise the search is not finished, and the gap is not reported, until every ranked candidate has been searched or recorded as unavailable.

MUSCOVITE-CENSUS-SETTLER-ORIGIN-RECOVERY.quote: Every stated origin is kept as testimony until a matching departure-side entry is found.

MYHERITAGE-DNA-MATCH-INVESTIGATION-01.quote: Save empty results with their actual query, kit, filters and date. Do not fill an unshown DNA measurement with zero or infer that a person outside the list has no shared DNA.

MYHERITAGE-HISTORICAL-RECORD-SEARCH-01.quote: Preserve the sparse baseline before tightening it. If a tighter query fails, relax one condition at a time and record the reason; changing everything together conceals what excluded the record.

NAZI-ERA-ANCESTRY-PROOF-RECORDS-01.quote: Their racial categories are the regime's classifications and are never evidence of anything about a person. Their entries were copied from parish and civil registers and must be checked against those registers.

NEWSPAPERS-COM-SEARCH-RECOVERY-01.quote: A surname can occur in one item and a travel verb in another on the same page. Confirm the subject and event within the actual item before assigning that event to the searched person.

OLD-BELIEVER-SECTARIAN-RECORD-RECOVERY-0.quote: Use this recipe when a Russian-Empire family suspected of Old Belief (раскол, старообрядчество) or Edinoverie (единоверие) is missing from the ordinary Orthodox metrical books, revision lists or confession rolls. Do not conclude that the family went unrecorded.

ORTHODOX-CLERGY-RECORD-RECOVERY-01.quote: Use it before you search metrical books or a present-day oblast archive, and before you merge or split clergy who share a surname.

PERIODICAL-INDEX-SEARCH-RETRIEVAL-01.quote: A personal-name miss therefore usually means the article text was never searched, and a hit is only a citation.

POLISH-INDEX-ORIGINAL-RECORD-RECOVERY-01.quote: A register description establishes a lead to holdings, not that the target entry has been inspected. Preserve the complete reference, not just a short number detached from its archive and fonds.

PORTUGUESE-PARISH-CIVIL-REGISTER-RECOVER.quote: Use it before you treat Portuguese records like Spanish or Hispanic ones. That mistake leads to four failures: searching a civil register that did not cover the person, looking in the wrong archive, reading the first surname as the father's, and calling a book missing when another archive holds it.

PROBATE-CASE-DOCUMENT-INVENTORY-01.quote: Keep a case inventory and a queue of unresolved references, so finding one useful document does not silently finish the estate search.

PUBLISHED-BOOK-CATALOGUE-AND-FULL-TEXT-D.quote: A miss is only a miss for that tool, query and range. It never establishes that the book doesn't exist or isn't held.

QUAKER-MEETING-RECORD-RECOVERY-01.quote: Before relying on Hinshaw, check that it covers the meeting. Decode the entry's meeting before you assign it to a place.

RABBINIC-LITERATURE-PERSON-SEARCH-01.quote: Keep two questions apart: did the ancestor exist, and is the bridge from your person to that ancestor documented? Rabbinic books often answer the first and rarely prove the second.

REPOSITORY-PHOTOGRAPH-COLLECTION-SEARCH-.quote: Do not compare faces yourself and do not name anyone from appearance. Resemblance is never evidence on its own: a recognition stays an attributed claim until documents support it.

RESEARCH-DOCUMENTATION-01.quote: Use `NIL` for a completed search with no hits. Record inaccessible images, interrupted searches and unsearched collections with their actual status.

ROOTSMAGIC-TREE-RECONCILIATION-WORKFLOW-.quote: Choose the destination and operation for each object, then inspect the saved result.

RUSSIAN-EMPIRE-EMIGRANT-ORIGIN-RECOVERY-.quote: Preserve the wording and field role until the movement and locality evidence resolve them.

RUSSIAN-EMPIRE-JEWISH-IDENTITY-ATTRIBUTI.quote: **A name mismatch never changes the branch verdict on its own; the household chain does.** Chain the person through household number → previous household number → age at previous revision → "выбыло" column → additional lists before you interpret any name.

RUSSIAN-EMPIRE-JEWISH-METRICAL-BOOK-RECO.quote: Do not search for "the village's" or "the synagogue's" metrical book. Having synagogues, or a sizeable Jewish population, does not show that a place had its own crown rabbi.

RUSSIAN-ESTATE-REGISTRATION-STATUS-01.quote: **A town mark on мещанин or купец names the society of registration, not the birthplace or residence.**

RUSSIAN-HOUSEHOLD-LIST-TRANSCRIPTION-AUD.quote: **Record what the image says, even against other years.**

RUSSIAN-IMPERIAL-SERVICE-RECORD-RECOVERY.quote: Do not stop at metrical books, revision lists or a military archive. A man in state service had his career and family written up in a formulary or service list (формулярный / послужной список).

RUSSIAN-MILITARY-REPRESSION-RECORD-EPISO.quote: an award order after a missing report does not, by itself, establish survival between those dates. Obtain an event-specific source before extending a life or death interval.

RUSSIAN-ORTHODOX-CONFESSION-LIST-READING.quote: The common errors are to read one year as a census, to turn an age into a birth year, to treat a household number as an identifier, and to treat a list entry as proof of a marriage, a parent or a death.

RUSSIAN-ORTHODOX-METRICAL-BOOK-RECOVERY-.quote: Read marriage-count formulae literally, treat margin decrees as separate dated events, and treat names and patronymics as hypotheses rather than proof of descent.

RUSSIAN-REVISION-LIST-HOUSEHOLD-CHAINING.quote: Record each copy as a separate observation of one episode, never as corroboration.

RUSSIAN-VILLAGE-FAMILY-RECONSTITUTION-01.quote: **A surname is a hint, not an identifier.**

RUSSIAN-VOLOST-TOWN-ADMINISTRATION-RECOR.quote: The common mistake is to send the researcher only to church registers and revision lists. That misses the local administrative fonds.

SCANDINAVIAN-PARISH-RECORD-RECOVERY-01.quote: Follow the family by farm or residence and by page cross-reference, not by patronymic. Settle identity at the household level.

SCANDINAVIAN-PATRONYMIC-FARM-NAME-RECORD.quote: The name in the parish register is usually not the American surname. Same-named parishioners are common, so separate them by birth date, parents, spouse, farm and vaccination entries, never by name alone.

SCHOOL-UNIVERSITY-RECORD-RECOVERY-01.quote: A compiled or published list is a lead with limited coverage. Absence from it does not show that the person never attended.

SCOTTISH-PARISH-STATUTORY-RECORD-RECOVER.quote: Treat register gaps and unsearched denominations as coverage still to search, not as proof the event did not happen.

SOURCE-CITATION-01.quote: An index entry and an inspected original image have different retrieval paths; record which one you used.

SOVIET-PERSONAL-FILE-RECOVERY-01.quote: Keep questionnaires (анкеты) and autobiographies found there as dated self-reports, and keep catalogue hits found by name as candidates.

SPANISH-CIVIL-PARISH-RECORD-ROUTING-01.quote: **Expect the national Registro Civil only from 1 January 1871.**

STATE-LEGISLATIVE-PRIVATE-ACT-PETITIONS-.quote: search the state's index of legislative acts, gather every entry that shares the hit's locator, and then retrieve the act and the petition or application behind it.

SURNAME-DISTRIBUTION-LOCALITY-LEADS-01.quote: It turns time-sliced maps, attestation dictionaries, a couple's surname overlap and country-wide counts into a **ranked, bounded list of localities to search**. It never produces an origin finding.

SWEDISH-MILITARY-RECORD-ROUTING-01.quote: Swedish military records are not one searchable pool. Each index covers one series, one branch and one period, so classify the man first and read every miss against the coverage of the index you searched.

TAX-ROLL-OBSERVATION-WORKFLOW-01.quote: Check each year against the liability rules in force then, and record every change as a bounded interval.

UK-CENSUS-AND-1939-REGISTER-INTERPRETATI.quote: Before reading any value, settle what that year's image is, who wrote the value, what night or day it refers to and what the year covers.

UNKNOWN-PARENTAGE-WATO-01.quote: WATO assumes single-path descent. Pedigree collapse / endogamy / a match related through two lines silently invalidates the score — the tool has no way to know and will still rank confidently.

WATO-01.quote: **The output is a set of competing hypotheses with *relative* odds — never a verdict.**

WATO-04.quote: When interpreting a reported ranking, ask whether pedigree collapse, endogamy or more than one relationship path could apply to these matches; do not replace the question with a generic warning.

US-20TH-CENTURY-MILITARY-SERVICE-RECONST.quote: Do not claim that the records burned and nothing survives.

US-CENSUS-PRACTICAL-WORKFLOWS-01.quote: Preserve the original census locator and keep literal observations separate from calculations and proposed identities.

US-CHURCH-RECORD-CUSTODY-01.quote: Before searching, work out the exact denominational branch, the record types that branch kept, the congregation or minister who kept the entry, and who holds those registers now. Do not report "not found" or "records lost" until that custody path has been checked.

US-CIVIL-WAR-SERVICE-RECORD-EPISODES-01.quote: It prevents four common errors: treating registration as service, giving the soldier every battle his regiment fought, guessing a transfer's date or meaning, and treating a database miss as proof of non-service.

US-FEDERAL-COURT-CASE-FILE-RECOVERY-01.quote: Decide whether the matter is federal before you search a county courthouse or a large genealogy database.

US-FEDERAL-LAND-ENTRY-FILE-RECOVERY-01.quote: The digitized GLO item is the final grant or warrant image, often a single page. It is not the entry file.

US-FREEDPEOPLE-RECORD-RECOVERY-01.quote: Surname, enslaver, list order and DNA signals stay separate hypotheses until a record names the person.

US-MILITARY-PENSION-FILE-RECOVERY-01.quote: Preserve the distinction between an index, a service record, a pension file and an abbreviated copy product.

US-MILITARY-SERVICE-TYPE-RECORD-ROUTING-.quote: The usual failure is to search only federal compiled-service or pension indexes and then report "no service". A related mistake is reading an empty donation-land or bounty-land search as meaningful when the man was never eligible.

US-PERIOD-LAW-RECORD-READING-01.quote: A rule shows what was required or allowed. It does not show what happened in one family.

US-TRIBAL-ENROLLMENT-RECORD-RECOVERY-01.quote: A rejection alone neither shows nor rules out Native descent.

US-VITAL-REGISTRATION-COVERAGE-01.quote: The usual mistake is to treat the statewide mandate year as the first year of coverage, search one certificate index for one county, and report a negative. Before any absence statement, build a register with one row for each registration authority and each separate series.

USA-IMMIGRATION-SEARCH-RECOVERY-01.quote: The recurring mistake is treating a search miss as a missing ancestor when the failure lies in the selected port, date, recorded name, image, citizenship history or custodian.

WIKITREE-DNA-TESTER-LINKS-01.quote: Do not mark a relationship DNA-confirmed solely because a tester appears in a list or because the external tree link works.

XDNA-PHASING-JUDGMENT-01.quote: **Ban invented small-segment statistics.** Any false-positive-rate or chance-match number must be attributed to a specific company/study (23andMe 2014, AncestryDNA 2020, FTDNA's Family Finder Matching 5.0) — never a smoothed or averaged figure presented as a universal law.

YDNA-MTDNA-INTERPRETATION-01.quote: **you do not compute or assign haplogroups, TMRCAs, or NPE verdicts from your own reasoning.** Every such value is a *hypothesis to route to the right tool or corroborate* — never a fact to state.

Y-01.quote: A GD is *stochastic*, not a clock (below).

Y-02.quote: **you do not compute or assign haplogroups, TMRCAs, or NPE verdicts from your own reasoning.**
